# Spec: github-project-board
<!-- Generated by /hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-11-04 -->

## Overview

A GitHub Projects (v2) board becomes a full lane board. `/hef.orchestrate`, `/hef.ship` and the stage lanes can
then run from a Project's issues, instead of a tasks-repo markdown board. Today a `github-project` board only feeds
the status brief. Every item-level mode the lanes call stops with "unsupported for github-project in Phase 1
(tasks-repo only)" (`status-board.sh:599-600`). `ledger.sh register` hard-codes `--kind tasks-repo`
(`ledger-lanes.sh:27,30`). And the orchestrator is told that a `github` board "can only be read"
(`hef.orchestrate.md:87`).

**Person's decisions** (forms, 2026-11-04):

1. The RFC stays a **file in the repo**. The issue body links it with an `rfc: docs/rfcs/<ID>.md` line: versioned,
   reviewed in PRs, and hash-pinned by the plan.
2. The lanes **move the card**. On each state change, `ledger.sh publish` sets the Project's Status field and posts
   one short issue comment.
3. The work is built before the four-lane test, and lanes use the GitHub Project as their board.

**Decided here by best practice:**

- An item is an Issue on the Project; draft items and pull requests are ignored.
- The id is `<prefix>-<issue number>`, with no second numbering.
- The columns are values of the Status single-select field.
- Kinds come from labels.
- Every `gh` failure fails closed.
- Only bash, jq and gh are used.

## User Scenarios

### US1: The orchestrator registers todo issues from a Project [P1]

- **Given** a config `{"source": "github-project", "owner": "<org>", "project": <n>, "repo": "<org>/<repo>",
  "id_prefix": "BC", "columns": {"todo": "Todo", "doing": "In Progress", "review": "In Review", "done": "Done",
  "backlog": "Backlog"}}`, and three issues whose Status is Todo
- **When** the orchestrator runs `status-board.sh --list todo`, then `ledger.sh register <id> --ref todo#<id>` for
  each id
- **Then**:
  - `--list todo` prints `BC-41`, `BC-42` and `BC-57`, one per line;
  - each `register` creates an entry with `source.kind: github-project`, `source.url: <issue url>`, the issue
    body's sha256, and the kind from its labels.
- **Edge:** a draft item or a pull request in the Todo column is not listed. A Project holding issues from two
  repos lists only the configured repo's issues.
- **Error:** `gh` is not authenticated, lacks the `read:project` scope, or the Project does not exist. `--list`
  exits non-zero and names the fix (`gh auth refresh -s read:project`). It never prints an empty list at exit 0.
- **Negative:** an id that names no issue on the Project is refused by every item mode, and so is an id whose
  id carries another prefix. Nothing is created.
- Files: `hooks/status-board.sh`, `hooks/board-github.sh` (new), `hooks/ledger-lanes.sh`, `tests/smoke-github-board.sh` (new).

### US2: A lane reads an issue as untrusted data [P1]

- **Given** a registered item `BC-42`, whose issue body holds an HTML comment and an `rfc: docs/rfcs/BC-42.md` line
- **When** a lane runs `status-board.sh --item BC-42`, `--item-raw BC-42`, `--item-kind BC-42` and `--item-rfc BC-42`
- **Then**:
  - `--item` prints `## BC-42 — <title>` and the body, with comments stripped, inside a nonce
    `<<<untrusted-begin … untrusted-end>>>` block, byte-shaped like a tasks-repo item;
  - `--item-raw` prints the same heading and body as written, which the ledger hashes;
  - `--item-kind` prints `incident` for a configured `bug` label, else `feature`;
  - `--item-rfc` prints the RFC path under the same rules as tasks-repo: a plain relative `.md` file inside
    `orchestrate.rfc_dir`, no `..`, no symlink, and the file must exist.
- **Edge:** a body edited on GitHub after claim gives a different sha256. The launch blocks with "item text changed
  since claim", as on tasks-repo. A body with CRLF line ends hashes the same on every read.
- **Error:** an issue whose body names two `rfc:` lines is refused ("one item, one RFC").
- **Negative:** text in the title, the body or a label never reaches a model outside the delimiters.
- Files: `hooks/board-github.sh`, `tests/smoke-github-board.sh`.

### US3: Only trusted authors' issues are taken automatically [P1]

- **Given** an issue opened or last edited by an account whose association with the repo is not `OWNER`,
  `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR`
- **When** it is registered
- **Then** the entry is created already blocked `human:intake`, naming the author's association. A person reads it
  and clears it with the existing `unblock`.
- **Edge:** `orchestrate.trusted_associations` widens the set (for example adding `CONTRIBUTOR`). It can never
  include `NONE`.
- **Error:** the association cannot be read from `gh`. Registration refuses, failing closed.
- **Negative:** an outside account's issue, added to the Project, never reaches a planner unread.
- Files: `hooks/board-github.sh`, `hooks/ledger-lanes.sh`.

### US4: `/hef.ship` adds an issue to the Project [P1]

- **Given** the GitHub board above
- **When** `/hef.ship "export orders as CSV"` runs `status-board.sh --add "export orders as CSV" --rfc`
- **Then**:
  - it creates an issue in `repo` with that title and an `rfc: docs/rfcs/BC-<n>.md` body line, where `<n>` is the
    new issue's number;
  - it adds the issue to the Project with Status = the `todo` column;
  - it prints `BC-<n>`.
  - `--incident` adds the configured incident label.
- **Edge:** the title rules are the tasks-repo ones: one line, 3–120 characters, no `#`, no item id.
- **Error:** the issue is created but adding it to the Project fails. The command exits non-zero, naming the issue
  URL, so a person can add it by hand. It never prints an id for an item that is not on the board.
- **Negative:** `--add` never edits an existing issue.
- Files: `hooks/board-github.sh`, `commands/hef.ship.md`.

### US5: Publish moves the card and comments [P2]

- **Given** `orchestrate.publish: true` and an entry whose phase moves from `plan` to `implement`
- **When** the orchestrator runs `ledger.sh publish BC-42`
- **Then**:
  - the card's Status becomes the column the state maps to: plan, build and blocked → `doing`, pr → `review`,
    merged/released → `done`;
  - one issue comment states the phase and the block.
  - Nothing is written when the state did not change.
- **Edge:** the Project has no option named like a mapped column. The command refuses, naming the missing option
  and the options that exist.
- **Error:** the token lacks the `project` scope. The refusal names `gh auth refresh -s project`, and the entry's
  `published` stays unchanged, so the next pass retries.
- **Negative:** publish never changes any field but Status, and never closes or edits an issue.
- Files: `hooks/ledger.sh` (publish), `hooks/board-github.sh`.

### US6: The orchestrator adopts a GitHub board [P2]

- **Given** a project with no `.claude/project-status.json`, whose repo has a GitHub Project
- **When** `/hef.orchestrate` runs `status-board.sh --detect`
- **Then** the `github` candidate lists the repo's Projects (owner, number, title) as boards the lanes can use. The
  orchestrator writes the `github-project` config for the one the person picks, with the column mapping read from
  the Project's Status options.
- **Negative:** the text "can only be read (/hef.status); dispatch needs a tasks board" is gone.
- Files: `hooks/status-board.sh`, `commands/hef.orchestrate.md`.

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | `status-board.sh --list <column>` prints the ids of a column's items, one per line, for both sources. For a github-project board: the Issues whose Status is the column's mapped value, in the configured repo. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | Item ids on a github-project board are `<id_prefix>-<issue number>`, for the issues of the one configured `repo`. Issues of other repos on the same Project are ignored. An id resolves to exactly one issue on the Project, or is refused. A github-project board is in-repo only: several repos and an external github board (routing by `--item-repo`) are out of scope until routing is specced. | P1 | US1, US2 |
| FR-003 | `--item` / `--item-raw` for github-project: the heading `## <id> — <title>` plus the body with CRLF normalised. `--item` strips HTML comments and wraps the text in the nonce untrusted delimiters; `--item-raw` prints it as written. | P1 | US2 |
| FR-004 | `--item-kind` for github-project: labels mapped by `kinds_labels` (default `bug`, `incident` → incident; `security` → vulnerability), else feature. | P1 | US2 |
| FR-005 | `--item-rfc` for github-project applies the tasks-repo RFC rules unchanged to the body's `rfc:` line, resolved under the board's top. | P1 | US2 |
| FR-006 | `ledger.sh register` records `--kind github-project --url <issue url>` for a github-project board, with the body hash and kind as for tasks-repo. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-007 | Registration creates the entry already blocked `human:intake` when the issue's author has an association outside `trusted_associations` (default OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR; `NONE` never allowed), or when its last editor is another account that is not a repo collaborator (GraphQL exposes no editor association, so the editor is checked with the collaborators API). The entry is never left unblocked, even when a step fails. | P1 | US3 |
| FR-008 | `--add <title> [--rfc \| --body-file <f>] [--incident]` creates one new item in the todo column, for both sources. `--rfc` and `--body-file` are mutually exclusive: a feature gets the `rfc:` line, a bug fix its description. For github-project: the issue in `repo` (with the description from `--body-file`; with `--rfc`, an `rfc: <dir>/<prefix>-<number>.md` body written to that new issue once its number is known), added to the Project with Status = todo, and the id printed. On tasks-repo, a description line that would start a heading is refused. A failure after creation exits non-zero, naming the issue URL. | P1 | US4 |
| FR-009 | Every gh read or write fails closed with the cause and the fix. No mode prints an empty answer at exit 0 for an error. | P1 | US1–US5 |
| FR-010 | `ledger.sh publish` on a github-project entry sets the Project's Status to the state's mapped column through `gh project item-edit`, and posts one comment. A missing option or scope refuses, leaving `published` unchanged. | P2 | US5 |
| FR-011 | `--detect` lists the repo's Projects. `/hef.orchestrate`'s adoption text offers a github-project board as a lane board, mapping the columns from its Status options. | P2 | US6 |
| FR-012 | Docs (`docs/install.md`, `docs/quickstart.md`) and `--check` describe the github-project board config, the scopes (`read:project` for reads; `project` for `--add` and publish), the column map, and the author trust rule. | P2 | US1–US6 |

### Negative requirements (what must NOT happen)

| ID | Must not happen | Scenario |
|----|-----------------|----------|
| NR-001 | A gh error, a missing scope or an unreadable Project is read as "no items" or "no item". | US1 |
| NR-002 | Issue title, body or label text reaches a model outside the untrusted delimiters, or a body edited after claim launches a stage. | US2 |
| NR-003 | An issue authored or last edited by an untrusted association is taken by a stage without a person's clear. | US3 |
| NR-004 | A gh write happens outside `--add` and `ledger.sh publish`, or publish changes anything but the Status field and one comment. | US4, US5 |
| NR-005 | An id resolves to an issue in another repo than the configured one, or to two issues. | US1 |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | Every item mode the lanes call works on a github-project board with the tasks-repo output shapes. | `tests/smoke-github-board.sh` with a named fake gh (`FakeGhProject`); one mutant per fail-closed path |
| SC-002 | A four-lane project runs one item from a real GitHub Project: register → plan → build → PR, with the card moving to In Review. | A person-run live test in a lanes project |
| SC-003 | The tasks-repo board behaves exactly as before. | The existing smoke suite passes unchanged |

## Clarifications

- Decided (person, 2026-11-04): the RFC is a repo file linked by an `rfc:` line; publish moves the Status field
  and comments.
- Decided here: the id uses the issue number, so no counter can drift. One board serves one repo (FR-002), so an id
  is never ambiguous.
- Decided here: a `review` column (In Review) is a new optional mapping, used only by publish. Without it, pr maps
  to `doing`.
